records.description_rewritten: Britzer Garten is a landscaped, paid-entry family park in Berlin-Britz with controlled entrances, ticket offices and seasonal gate times. Planet Randy alleges frequent late-evening cruising, yet its only dated entry (8 June 2023) is a proposal to meet at night, not a verified visit. The official operator says the gates close, with automated admission in November–February only until 18:00 and the grounds closing about an hour later. Its night-time claims are therefore not supported for ordinary opening conditions.

supplemental_sources.note: One 2023 meet-up question, undated editorial sexual-use claims.
Official gates, paid entry and seasonal hours including November 2026.
Operator confirms Nov 2026 winter entry hours and events.

older_posts.note: No report of completed visit or cruising.

records.access_information: Ticketed botanical and family garden. Public access only during scheduled hours or special ticketed events; night entry otherwise not supported. No permission for sex.
possible_duplicates_and_flags: Original source 'late evenings' conflicts with gated opening model.
Significant children/family use; no verified recent cruising.

records.description_rewritten: Arkenberg quarry pond is a Planet Randy label for Arkenberger Baggersee, also called Arkenberger Kieskuhle, in Berlin-Pankow. This is the same named gravel lake previously recorded under GS2-DE-BERLIN-001 at index 626; retain this record in research and mark it an almost certain duplicate for filtering. Berlin's official lake page states a general swimming ban for insufficient water cleanliness, contradicting the directory's positive description as a bathing lake. No credible recent cruising visit can be attributed to this separate entry.

supplemental_sources.note: Primary source article identifies Arkenberger Baggersee and alternate Arkenberger Kieskuhle.
City page says general swimming ban and two gravel lakes.

records.access_information: Public recreation paths as signed, and swimming prohibited by city source. Industrial/quarry sections and the landfill area may be restricted.
possible_duplicates_and_flags: Likely exact duplicate of queue #626 GS2-DE-BERLIN-001.
Municipal general bathing ban; do not describe as safe swimming.

records.description_rewritten: People's Park Prenzlauer Berg is the English-rendered name of Volkspark Prenzlauer Berg. Planet Randy explicitly directs visitors to the small grove reached from Judith-Auer-Straße, the same subarea and entrance named by GS2-DE-BERLIN-060 at index 674. That other source contains dated June–July 2026 first-person visits, but Planet Randy itself has no reviews or independent activity verification. Retain the candidate as a duplicate lead, not a new different park.

Independent public-park identity and entrance, not cruising proof.

Planet Randy gives address Naumannstraße 55 and claims the urinal has no door and is continuously accessible, but that operational assertion is undated and not officially checked in 2026. Its page has zero reviews.

records.description_rewritten: Thomashöhe is a hilly public neighbourhood park along Thomasstraße in Neukölln. Planet Randy mentions the slope/park entrance by Thomasstraße and Mittelweg, matching the earlier 'Park Thomasstraße' candidate GS2-DE-BERLIN-031 at index 653. The gay-directory editorial claims very busy weekday evenings, but it has zero reviews and no dates; the other archived source has historic rather than 2026 eyewitness remarks. Do not treat it as an independent recent confirmation.
